questions.question: What is the approximate cold-start time for a 70B model going from cold to serving without any mitigation?
questions.explanation: The lesson states a raw 70B cold start takes 3-8 minutes. For a 7B model it is 5-10 minutes; for 70B it can exceed 20 minutes. In a serverless context, that is an outage, not a warm-up.

questions.question: What is Modal's published cold-start floor with GPU memory snapshots enabled?
questions.explanation: Modal publishes 2-4 second cold starts as their floor, achieved via GPU memory checkpointing. Baseten's default is 5-10 seconds, dropping to sub-second with pre-warming.

questions.question: Why does live migration transfer input tokens rather than KV cache when moving a running request to a new instance?
options: KV cache is encrypted and cannot be transferred between instances
Input tokens are kilobytes while KV cache is gigabytes, so transferring tokens is orders of magnitude cheaper
The KV cache format is instance-specific and cannot be decoded by another instance
Input tokens are always cached at the gateway layer so re-transfer is free
questions.explanation: Input tokens are kilobytes; the KV cache for a long conversation can be gigabytes. Live migration sends the small token payload and accepts the penalty of recomputing prefill on the new instance rather than transferring the large KV cache.

questions.question: ServerlessLLM's tiered loading pipeline moves weights through which sequence of storage tiers?
questions.explanation: ServerlessLLM implements a NVMe → DRAM → HBM tiered pipeline, achieving 10-200x latency reduction versus downloading weights cold. The hierarchy matches storage bandwidth: NVMe is faster than network, DRAM is faster than NVMe, HBM is fastest.

questions.question: When should min_workers > 0 (warm pool) be mandated versus when is scale-to-zero acceptable?
options: Always mandate warm pools regardless of workload type
Warm pools for SLO-critical interactive paths; scale-to-zero acceptable for background batch paths tolerating 5-10 minute cold starts
Scale-to-zero for all production paths; warm pools only for development environments
Warm pools only for models over 70B; scale-to-zero for smaller models
questions.explanation: The lesson's warm-pool math: high-value interactive paths (chat, voice agents) need min_workers=1-2 to avoid SLO breaches. Background batch paths (nightly classification) can tolerate 5-10 minute cold starts since they are not user-facing.

questions.question: What speedup does the Run:ai Model Streamer provide for weight loading versus standard sequential loading?
questions.explanation: The Run:ai Model Streamer achieves approximately 2x weight-load speedup by streaming weights asynchronously while the model begins initialization. It is Layer 2 in the five-layer cold-start mitigation stack.
